reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Indication: osteopenia, follow-up. Comparison: 06/14/2023, same scanner. L1-L4 BMD T-score -1.4. Left femoral neck T-score -2.1. Left total hip T-score -1.8. Decrease at the femoral neck and total hip exceeds the least significant change. No levels excluded. FRAX (femoral neck BMD, no prior fracture, no parental hip fracture, no glucocorticoids, nonsmoker, no alcohol, BMI 23): 10-year probability of major osteoporotic fracture 14%, hip fracture 3.2%.
reports.conclusion: Low bone mass (osteopenia) with significant decline at the hip since 2023. Ten-year hip fracture probability 3.2% meets the treatment threshold of 3% or greater.

documents.title: Bone Density Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Carolyn, your bone density is still in the osteopenia range, but the hip has dropped since 2023 (femoral neck -2.1, was -1.6). Your 10-year hip fracture risk is now 3.2%, which crosses the 3% line where treatment is recommended. I'd like to go over a weekly pill with you in person. The front desk will reach out to set up a visit.

documents.title: RE: Bone Density Result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I was afraid of that, with my mother's history. I booked Monday Dec 1. Should I bring anything?

documents.title: RE: Bone Density Result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Just bring the date of your last dental checkup and any questions. We'll draw a couple of labs that day.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once weekly on rising, with a full glass of plain water, at least 30 minutes before food, drink or other medicines. Stay upright for 30 minutes.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
71F here to discuss DXA 11/17/25.

DXA: femoral neck T -2.1 (from -1.6 in 2023), total hip -1.8 (from -1.3), spine -1.4. FRAX major 14%, hip 3.2%. No fractures, no height loss she knows of, no back pain. Family hx: mother osteoporosis, maternal aunt hip fracture at 78. Still walking daily, though the garden is put to bed for the winter.
Dental: cleaning in October, no extractions or implants planned. No reflux or swallowing problems.
Meds: none. NKDA.
Research PFTs 10/2025 normal for age per study letter.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight steady. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No thoracic or lumbar spinous tenderness. Gait steady.

A/P: Osteopenia, now with hip fracture probability above the treatment threshold.
- Reviewed options. She prefers a weekly pill. Alendronate 70 mg once weekly, 90-day supply. Went through dosing: first thing in the morning, full glass of plain water, nothing else for 30 minutes, stay upright. Rare jaw and thigh-bone problems discussed; tell her dentist she's on it.
- CMP and vitamin D today before she starts; start once I confirm calcium and kidney function are normal.
- Dietary calcium is adequate (daily yogurt, cheese). Continue walking; balance work.
- Plan DXA again in 2 years on treatment.
Follow up at AWV in spring.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Calcium, kidney function and vitamin D are all normal, so you're clear to start the alendronate. It's at your pharmacy. Pick a day of the week that's easy to remember.

documents.title: Question about the bone pill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Took my second one this morning (Wednesdays). No problems with my stomach. How long exactly do I have to wait for coffee? I've been holding out a full hour to be safe.

documents.title: RE: Question about the bone pill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thirty minutes is the minimum, an hour is even better for absorption, so you're doing it right. Plain water only with the pill, and stay sitting or standing until you eat. Glad it's agreeing with you.

documents.title: Refill: alendronate
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy request for alendronate 70 mg weekly, #12. Started 12/2025, tolerating per patient message. Refilled x1 per protocol, 90 days.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. 71F.

On alendronate weekly since early December, Wednesday mornings. No heartburn, no trouble swallowing, no jaw or thigh pain. Saw her dentist, who knows she's on it.
Memory: name recall about the same as last year, not worse. Still doing everything for herself, driving, managing her own bills and schedule.
Walking daily again now that the weather has turned. No falls.

HRA: independent in ADLs and IADLs. PHQ-2 0.
Meds: alendronate 70 mg weekly. NKDA.

MoCA 26/30, same as 4/2025.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight stable. Alert, fluent, good historian. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema. Spine nontender. Gait normal, single-leg stance steady.

A/P:
1. Osteopenia on alendronate: tolerating, good technique. Continue. DXA late 2027.
2. Age-related cognitive decline: stable, function intact. Recheck MoCA next year.
3. Health maintenance: Tdap today (last 2016). Annual CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c. Mammogram fall 2027. Flu and COVID in the fall.
RTC fall for alendronate check, then AWV next spring.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All normal this year as well: kidneys, calcium, liver, blood counts, cholesterol and A1c. Continue the alendronate as you are.

documents.title: Refill: alendronate
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Alendronate 70 mg weekly #12 refilled, 90-day supply. Seen 4/13, labs normal.

documents.title: Fall appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The doctor said to come back in the fall to check on the bone medicine. Could I have a Monday in late September? Mornings are best.

documents.title: RE: Fall appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: You're booked Monday, September 21 at 9:30. We can give your flu shot that day too if it's in by then.

documents.title: Refill: alendronate
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic refill request, alendronate 70 mg weekly. Refilled #12, 90 days. Follow-up already scheduled 9/21.
